title: Term-Based (BM25) and Embedding Retrieval
summary: There are two families of retriever. Sparse retrievers score documents by the words they share with the query, weighted by rarity (TF-IDF, BM25). Dense retrievers embed query and documents as vectors and compare meanings with cosine similarity. Each fails where the other succeeds.
objectives: Build an inverted index and score documents with TF-IDF by hand
Compute BM25 scores and explain what k1 (term-frequency saturation) and b (length normalisation) do
Compute cosine similarity between embeddings and explain why it captures paraphrase
Contrast bi-encoders and cross-encoders in accuracy and cost, with numbers
Explain how embedding models are trained with a contrastive loss and why hard negatives matter
prerequisites: You should have built the toy retriever in [How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture) and know what an embedding vector is ([Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings)). Logarithms and softmax ([Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling)) are used.
